proposals.relationship: Vovelle identifies Labrousse as the teacher who taught him historical and archival research within a social-history framework.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2005answers2–3 and17 explicitly identify Labrousse as his master and explain the passage through economic, conjunctural and social history. Tersen’s referral and the broader Marxist setting retain separate credit. Vovelle subsequently took distance from limits of this framework while keeping social history; no claim of total doctrinal obedience or later individual influence from Simiand simply because a comparison is invoked.

primary_locators.passage: Labrousse m’a donc introduit; celui qui m’a appris les techniques de la recherche historique.

proposals.relationship: Vovelle acknowledges Duby’s influence in the development of his history of mentalities.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2005answer17 explicitly names the proximity and influence of Georges Duby and Robert Mandrou;2 places the development of this history more with Mandrou/Duby than Braudel. Collective credit is preserved; Duby is not declared sole originator, and inheritance of a research centre alone is not the proof. Mandrou lacks an individual endpoint and is held with the same primary evidence.

primary_locators.passage: la proximité et l’influence de Georges Duby et puis de Robert Mandrou.

proposals.relationship: Vovelle uses Braudel’s long-duration account of mentalities to frame the question of change during revolutionary crisis.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1991article in2012reprint233–234 explicitly refers jointly to Mandrou’s longer time and Braudel’s long duration, then investigates their relation to abrupt revolutionary mutation. This is a named conceptual starting point, not proof of exclusive formative transmission or a blanket rejection of Braudel. Existing edge_1489 to Annales remains a separate group contribution; it is not retargeted.

primary_locators.passage: Les mentalités collectives, si l’on s’en réfère à Mandrou; ou à Braudel; peut-on changer les hommes en dix ans?

proposals.relationship: Vovelle names Marx’s writing among the basic reading in his early Marxist historical formation.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2005pp1–2 describes an elementary formation through teaching, manuals and basic books, naming La lutte des classes; the surviving idea was a totalizing history connecting economic, social and cultural levels. The transcript supplies no exact Marx edition, and none is invented. Marc Soriano, manuals and translation work are not erased; no claim of advanced Marxology or derivation of every mentalities argument.

primary_locators.passage: un certain nombre de livres de base comme La lutte des classes de Marx; De cette imprégnation marxiste.

proposals.relationship: Vovelle recalls using Gramsci in Les jacobins while qualifying how central that reading was to his own research.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2005pp6–7 says he exploited Gramsci in Les jacobins (note identifies1999 Les jacobins, de Robespierre à Chevènement) and had earlier assisted Moget with translation work. The latter is recollection, not a substitute translator credit:1959 Oeuvres choisies credits Moget and Armand Monjo, preface Cogniot, per2n2. Vovelle immediately qualifies the usefulness as yes and no; no exclusive or foundational influence claim and no original book read.

primary_locators.passage: j’aidais mon ami Gilbert Moget; mon petit livre sur les jacobins où je l’exploite quand même.

proposals.relationship: Vovelle regards Gramsci’s transhistorical Jacobinism as historically dated and limits its usefulness for his own historical inquiries.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2005p7 follows the acknowledgment of actual use: the transhistorical reading is itself a moment in historical reflection, and its utility for his existing research was yes and no. This specific limitation coexists with a resource arrow and does not reject all Gramsci, deny reading, or establish a contemporary direct exchange.

primary_locators.passage: la lecture du jacobinisme transhistorique de Gramsci m’apparaît historiquement datée.

proposals.relationship: Vovelle cites Althusser when describing a flexible economic grounding of total history.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2005p7 explicitly says he had read Althusser and refers to the ultimate economic justification while emphasizing flexibility as in Vilar;17 includes Althusser among later reading that brought him something after his path was already formed. Exact Althusser title or edition is not supplied. No original formative influence, rigid economic determinism or equivalence with Vilar’s whole argument is inferred.

primary_locators.passage: on a quand même lu Althusser; d’une façon extrêmement souple.

proposals.relationship: Vovelle treats Ariès’s diverse-source reconstruction of attitudes to death as an exemplary interlocutor for his own inquiry.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1976pp124 and127 calls the varied-source demonstration brilliant/exemplary and the global model a stimulus to problem formulation;132 calls Ariès his interlocutor and accomplice. Own2005p17 describes Ariès opening avenues in the maturation of a personal approach.1976p124 expressly argues qualitative and serial approaches are complementary; these debts coexist with concrete criticisms. The1974 English essay,1975 French collection and future definitive synthesis remain distinct; no whole book read.

la lecture globale et les conclusions
notre interlocuteur et complice

proposals.relationship: Vovelle argues that Ariès’s model gives too little explanatory weight to religious and ideological change in attitudes toward death.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1976pp129–131 questions material/spiritual reference systems, the privileging of a collective unconscious and idealized tamed origins, and the family explanation of silence in wills. He acknowledges possible overemphasis in his own treatment of Catholic reconquest, accepts some family mediation, and insists his criticism measures the book’s interest. This is a particular methodological disagreement, not a personal denunciation or claim that qualitative sources are invalid;124 explicitly defends complementary methods.

absence de référence religieuse; l’insistance est à la mesure de l’intérêt

proposals.relationship: Darnton reports Ariès’s alternative explanation of Vovelle’s testamentary findings through changed family trust rather than declining religious ritual.
proposals.evidence_note: Explicit named scholarly mediation in Darnton1974paragraph beginning Ariès tries to explain Vovelle’s data. This is a precise explanatory alternative, not proof Ariès rejected the archival findings or every dechristianization process. Vovelle’s own1976p131 acknowledges disagreement on this family explanation while sharing the importance of family mediation. Ariès’s underlying work remains unread; Darnton’s report is not silently promoted to a freshly read Ariès passage.

mutation des attitudes familiales rendant compte du silence.

proposals.relationship: Darnton praises Vovelle’s testamentary research but questions whether declining ritual proves dechristianization and how fully the change is explained.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1974review final paragraphs distinguish decline from extinction and suggest that abandoning baroque rites could signify religious purification. He also finds socio-economic change too general and some explanation circular, while praising the method as a major historical advance and acknowledging similar explanatory limits in other great theses. This is not a rejection of quantitative research or proof Vovelle asserted Christianity vanished; original monograph unread.

primary_locators.printed_pages: HTML paragraphs How this change; Ultimately; Dechristianization; Yet such criticism; final praise
primary_locators.passage: Dechristianization also poses a problem; The abandonment of baroque rites; Vovelle has supplied them.

proposals.relationship: Vovelle explicitly shares Delumeau’s emphasis on inherited magical thought in early modern religious behavior.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1976p122 states agreement on the weight of magical belief and ritual while discussing a justified criticism of Mourir autrefois and the difficulty of recovering practices from sources. The unnamed critic is not automatically Delumeau. This specific reverse resource differs from existing edge_2036 Vovelle-to-Delumeau and undirected methodological dialogue edge_2037; neither is duplicated or withdrawn. No claim of identical religious interpretations or whole-book reading.

primary_locators.passage: partageons sur ce point la lecture de Jean Delumeau.

proposals.relationship: Vovelle opposes reducing revolutionary history to an ideological history of texts and discourse associated with Furet.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2005pp14–15 frames his defense of total/global revolutionary history against what he describes as the Furet universe of ideological texts and discourse. He recognizes a conjunctural political dimension to his own bicentenary posture and also claims a wider opening of research; this is Vovelle’s retrospective characterization, not a neutral description of all Furet works. He reports an earlier critique of L’Atelier de l’histoire at11 but that review and the original Furet book are not read. No automatic reciprocal Furet-to-Vovelle arrow.

primary_locators.passage: Dans La galerie des ancêtres; non pas simplement circonscrite dans l’univers furétiste.

proposals.relationship: Vovelle compares his later encounter with Ginzburg to discovering historians independently posing simultaneous problems.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2005p17 describes discovery through parallel problem setting rather than a formative chance encounter;8–9 separately recognizes Italian/Ginzburg case-study initiatives while recalling US reception of his own work. This is an undirected methodological comparison, not evidence Ginzburg caused Vovelle’s established approach, that he read every microhistorical work, or that their methods coincide in full.

primary_locators.passage: les initiateurs ça a été Carlo Ginzburg; problèmes simultanés chacun dans son coin.
